Kernel coverage is incomplete or differs by browser. Compilation, numerical checks, isolated timings, and composite timings remain separate.
Some tuning calibrations were truncated. A valid model capture does not establish that every tuner completed or that its selected kernel is optimal.

Captures used an RTX 5070 Ti with NVIDIA driver 595.71.05 on a shared Linux workstation. Browser processes were isolated and GPU profiling was serialized; unrelated applications remained running. Host load and GPU telemetry are retained in the source captures.

The model table measures three deterministic text-request shapes in an on-page engine. It does not establish multi-question, batch, worker/UI, mobile, or camera sensor-to-screen performance. F32 packs were not available for this sweep.

All 82 registered kernels have compilation, numerical-check, and timestamp evidence in the union of the two browser runs. Coverage differs by browser: Firefox lacks subgroups; this Chromium build lacks shader-f16. Compatible compilation alone is never counted as numerical or timing evidence.

Isolated frozen-control comparisons use the same emitted shader implementation and establish repeatability for those fixtures. Independent CPU references and focused fusion/reference guards supplement them; they are not independent mathematical proof for every possible input.

SemIf 4B Q8 in Firefox exceeded the strict 0.0005 cross-load raw-probability tolerance, with maximum difference 0.0012237727642059326. Rounded public answers and binary choices were unchanged. Its independent upstream-reference guard passed on both browsers at the pre-existing Q8 tolerance of 0.022. The strict repeatability failure remains failed and has no passing timing row.

Gemma baseline/candidate ABBA runs retained identical probabilities and choices in the authored decision replay and no unprofiled latency regression. Observed profiled GPU-total changes were below the 5 percent promotion threshold. The stable shape-level matrix gains are not claimed as application-latency gains; broader load-time calibration can add initial tuning work within the same deadline.

The loaded Gemma E2B BF16 vision companion passed its rectangular 64-soft-token reference fixture on both browsers, with maximum absolute error 0.00001990795135498047. Separate unprofiled tower medians were 100 ms in Firefox and 25.1 ms in Chromium; diagnostic GPU totals were 23.397 ms and 21.386 ms. These are vision-tower measurements, not full image-decision latency or camera FPS.

Kev 9B BF16 could not upload in Firefox because of GPU memory exhaustion; it was measured in Chromium. Clef BF16 had no local pack. No model weights were downloaded by the profiling runners or included in the public report.
